title: Meet the Kit
description: Hit each of the 8 pads, hear what it sounds like, and find out what drummers use it for.

steps.title: What's on the kit
steps.description:
You've got 8 pads, laid out in two rows. Here's what each one is:

• KCK (kick): the big bass drum a drummer plays with their foot. It's the thump you feel in your chest.
• SNR (snare): the sharp crack that answers the kick.
• CHH (closed hi-hat): two cymbals clamped shut, so you get a tight tick.
• OHH (open hi-hat): the same cymbals left loose, so they hiss and ring.
• CLP (clap): a hand clap, used a lot in pop, hip-hop and dance music.
• TOM (tom): a deeper drum with a bit of pitch, mostly for fills.
• CRS (crash): the loud splash you hear when a new section kicks in.
• RDE (ride): a big cymbal with a steady ping for keeping time.

We'll go through them one at a time.

steps.title: Start with the kick
steps.description: Hit the kick. Pretty much every beat is built around this sound, so get used to how low and round it is.
steps.hint: It's the red pad at the far left of the top row, labelled KCK.

steps.title: Now the snare
steps.description: Hit the snare. Where the kick thumps, the snare cracks. In most songs it lands on beats 2 and 4.
steps.hint: The orange pad right next to the kick, labelled SNR.

steps.title: Closed hi-hat
steps.description: Hit the closed hi-hat. It's short and tight, and drummers tap it over and over to keep the pulse moving.
steps.hint: Top row, third from the left. Look for CHH on the green pad.

steps.title: Open hi-hat
steps.description: Now the open hi-hat. Same cymbals, but they're left loose, so the sound hangs in the air a lot longer. Hit it and listen to it fade.
steps.hint: It's the last pad on the top row, labelled OHH.

steps.title: Clap
steps.description: Hit the clap. In pop and hip-hop it often sits on top of the snare or takes its place completely.
steps.hint: Bottom row, far left. Look for CLP.

steps.title: Tom
steps.description: Hit the tom. It's rounder than the snare and has more of a note to it. Drummers roll around the toms for fills, the little bursts that lead into the next part of a song.
steps.hint: Bottom row, second from the left, labelled TOM.

steps.title: Crash
steps.description: Hit the crash. It's big and it's loud, and that's the point: it tells everyone listening that a new section has started.
steps.hint: Bottom row, third from the left. It's the yellow pad labelled CRS.

steps.title: Ride
steps.description: Last one, the ride. It has a clear ping with a shimmer underneath. Drummers switch to it from the hi-hat when they want the beat to feel more open.
steps.hint: The pad in the bottom right corner, labelled RDE.

steps.title: Which one thumps?
steps.description: You want the deep, low sound that the rest of a beat is built on. Which pad do you reach for?
